structured.answer: I'm keeping the keren hishtalmut and not touching it: my employer puts in up to 7.5% and I put in 2.5%, and after 6 years I can take everything out tax free. If I take it out earlier I pay tax, and the page warns that's expensive. Still, the page's own example confused me, because it showed the keren only about 415 ₪ ahead of a regular account after 10 years.

stuck.why: I thought the keren was a big deal, but the example shows almost no gain. It also shows higher costs (2,402 ₪) and even tax (2,922 ₪) on something I understood to be tax free. I couldn't tell whether the employer's 7.5% is in there.
The '‎-342.02 ₪' made me think the keren could even lose money compared with the other option.
Nothing told me what to actually do first, like check my company or my track.

findings.what: The example shows the keren only 415 ₪ ahead after 10 years, with higher costs and tax. It makes the keren look not worth it, which goes against the opening paragraph. The employer's money doesn't seem to be in the example.
findings.where: Calculator result under 'מה מייחד קרן השתלמות'

findings.what: The big number 17,370 ₪ reads like the final amount. That it's only the profit is said in small grey text below it.
A minus sign in the range '‎-342.02 ₪ לבין 2,106 ₪' is scary and unexplained.
Tax of 2,922 ₪ is shown on a product the page calls tax free. The 300/200 split that explains it sits in dense text.
No 'what to do now' step for a salaried person who already has a keren through work
Jargon like 'הפקדה מוטבת' and 'הרווח הריאלי' is used before it's explained; the explanations are only in the glossary at the bottom.
